panels.title: Latency (ms) — Real-Time Apps
panels.description: Per-application latency for real-time communication apps over time. SOURCE: VictoriaMetrics metric 'fortigate_sdwan_sla_latency', labels app=~'Zoom|Microsoft_Teams|Google_Meet|Slack', site=norrsken-kigali. Derived from Elasticsearch index 'logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-*', field 'fortinet.firewall.latency' (float, milliseconds). Original FortiGate log: logid=0113022941, type=event, subtype=sdwan. Ingested via Elastic Agent Fortinet integration v1.36.8. Pushed to VictoriaMetrics every 60s by fortigate_sla_bridge.py. IMPORTANT: For Zoom, Teams, and Slack this measures the TCP signaling channel latency — not the UDP media stream. The actual video/audio RTP stream latency is measured separately in the Call Quality dashboard. Thresholds: Green <80ms, Yellow 80-150ms, Red >150ms.

panels.title: Jitter (ms) — Real-Time Apps
panels.description: Per-application jitter for real-time communication apps over time. SOURCE: VictoriaMetrics metric 'fortigate_sdwan_sla_jitter', labels app=~'Zoom|Microsoft_Teams|Google_Meet|Slack', site=norrsken-kigali. Derived from Elasticsearch field 'fortinet.firewall.jitter' (float, milliseconds). Original FortiGate log: logid=0113022941, type=event, subtype=sdwan. Pushed to VictoriaMetrics every 60s by fortigate_sla_bridge.py. Jitter = inter-packet delay variation measured by FortiGate kernel. IMPORTANT: Same TCP-only caveat as latency panel — this is signaling jitter for Zoom/Teams/Slack, not media stream jitter. Thresholds: Green <30ms, Yellow 30-100ms, Red >100ms.

panels.title: Packet Loss (%) — Real-Time Apps
panels.description: Per-application packet loss for real-time communication apps over time. SOURCE: VictoriaMetrics metric 'fortigate_sdwan_sla_packetloss', labels app=~'Zoom|Microsoft_Teams|Google_Meet|Slack', site=norrsken-kigali. Derived from Elasticsearch field 'fortinet.firewall.packetloss' (string, percent). Original FortiGate log: logid=0113022941, type=event, subtype=sdwan. Pushed to VictoriaMetrics every 60s by fortigate_sla_bridge.py. IMPORTANT: TCP-only measurement for Zoom/Teams/Slack signaling paths. Thresholds: Green <1%, Yellow 1-5%, Red >5%.

panels.title: Latency (ms) — Productivity Apps
panels.description: Per-application latency for productivity apps over time. SOURCE: VictoriaMetrics metric 'fortigate_sdwan_sla_latency', labels app=~'Gmail|Google_Drive|Google_Meet|YouTube|iCloud|Github|Claude', site=norrsken-kigali. Derived from Elasticsearch field 'fortinet.firewall.latency' (float, ms). Original FortiGate log: logid=0113022941, type=event, subtype=sdwan. AppID mapping built from correlating 'fortinet.firewall.appid' with 'network.application' across traffic logs (logid=0000000013). Pushed to VictoriaMetrics every 60s by fortigate_sla_bridge.py. Note: Y-axis may show large values due to passive SLA overflow artifacts (2^31 integer wrap) in historical data. Values above 5000ms are artifacts and filtered by the bridge — historical backfill may contain some.

panels.title: Current App Quality — Latency
panels.description: Table showing mean, max, and current latency per application. SOURCE: VictoriaMetrics metric 'fortigate_sdwan_sla_latency' reduced to mean/max/last over the selected time range. Derived from Elasticsearch field 'fortinet.firewall.latency'. Original FortiGate log: logid=0113022941, type=event, subtype=sdwan. Color coding: Green <80ms, Yellow 80-150ms, Red >150ms. Use 'Last' column for current network state. Use 'Mean' for baseline characterisation over longer time ranges. Apps with no recent traffic will not appear.

panels.title: All Apps — Latency Heatmap
panels.description: All named applications on one panel — latency heatmap over time. SOURCE: VictoriaMetrics metric 'fortigate_sdwan_sla_latency', all labels except SSL/TLS generics and unknown apps, site=norrsken-kigali. Filter: app!~'SSL|SSL_TLSv1_2|SSL_TLSv1_3|Unknown|app_0|app_16195'. Derived from Elasticsearch field 'fortinet.firewall.latency'. Original FortiGate log: logid=0113022941, type=event, subtype=sdwan. AppID to name mapping in fortigate_sla_bridge.py APPID_NAMES dictionary. Each app appears as a separate colored line. Useful for identifying which specific app degrades first during network events.

panels.title: x3 Interface Throughput (bps)
panels.description: Real-time TX and RX throughput on x3 — the FortiGate WAN interface connecting to the Peplink Balance 1350. SOURCE: VictoriaMetrics metrics 'fortigate_interface_tx_rate_bps' and 'fortigate_interface_rx_rate_bps', label interface=port16. Derived from FortiGate REST API endpoint: GET https://192.168.1.1/api/v2/monitor/system/interface (authenticated via Bearer token, API admin account). Fields used: 'tx_bytes', 'rx_bytes' — delta calculated between polls. Formula: rate_bps = (current_bytes - previous_bytes) * 8 / poll_interval_sec. Polled every 30 seconds by fortigate_interface_collector.py. IMPORTANT: port16 negotiates at 100 Mbps. If aggregate WAN capacity (Fiber1 + Fiber2 + Starlink) exceeds 100 Mbps, this link is the bottleneck. Threshold lines at 80 Mbps (yellow) and 95 Mbps (red) indicate congestion risk.

panels.title: port16 Link Status
panels.description: Current link state per active FortiGate interface. SOURCE: VictoriaMetrics metric 'fortigate_interface_link', all interfaces, site=norrsken-kigali. Derived from FortiGate REST API endpoint: GET https://192.168.1.1/api/v2/monitor/system/interface Field: 'link' (boolean) → converted to 1 (UP) or 0 (DOWN). Polled every 30 seconds by fortigate_interface_collector.py. Only UP interfaces are reported — DOWN interfaces with no traffic are excluded to reduce noise. System interfaces (mgmt, ha, ssl.root) are always excluded. Green = UP, Red = DOWN. Any red panel indicates a physical link failure.

panels.title: x3 Negotiated Speed
panels.description: Negotiated link speed on x3 in Mbps. SOURCE: VictoriaMetrics metric 'fortigate_interface_speed_mbps', label interface=port16, site=norrsken-kigali. Derived from FortiGate REST API endpoint: GET https://192.168.1.1/api/v2/monitor/system/interface Field: 'speed' (float, Mbps as reported by the interface). Polled every 30 seconds by fortigate_interface_collector.py. Currently shows 100 Mbps — the negotiated speed between FortiGate port16 and the Peplink Balance 1350 LAN port. If this changes (e.g. drops to 10 Mbps), it indicates a physical layer negotiation problem between the two devices.
